sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson you learn to talk about the future: a plan you have made, something about to happen, a meeting you have fixed. There are two ways to say it, and you already know half of each.

examples.en: I am going to descale the kettle.
The sink is going to overflow.
examples.translation: I can see it is about to happen

examples.en: I am meeting the carer tomorrow.

sections.title: going to — a plan you have decided

blocks.text: When you have already decided to do something, say am / is / are going to + the action as in the dictionary: I am going to repaint the wall. The clip and to are both needed.

examples.en: I am going to descale the kettle.
examples.translation: I have decided to clean it

examples.en: She is going to repaint the wall.
We are going to alter the dress.
examples.translation: we plan to change its size

examples.en: I am going to hang the bunting.
examples.translation: I plan to put up the flags

fixes.wrong: I going to descale the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

fixes.wrong: I am going descale the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

fixes.wrong: I am going to descaling the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

drill.why: After going you always need to.

sections.title: going to — you can see it coming

blocks.text: Use the same form when the signs are already in front of you: the water is at the edge — The sink is going to overflow; the tower is leaning — The tower is going to topple.

examples.en: The sink is going to overflow.
The tower is going to topple.
The shelf is going to collapse.
The jumper is going to shrink.
examples.translation: it is in a hot wash

examples.en: The boards are going to rot.
examples.translation: they are wet all the time

fixes.right: The tower is going to topple.

fixes.wrong: The boards is going to rot.
fixes.right: The boards are going to rot.

drill.question: The water in the sink is right at the edge and the tap is still on. What do you say?
drill.optionB: The sink is going to overflow.
drill.explain: You can see it is about to happen: is going to.

sections.title: An arrangement: I am meeting… tomorrow

blocks.text: When you have agreed with someone and there is a time — tomorrow at six — use the form from lesson 9: am / is / are + -ing and the time. I am meeting the carer tomorrow. Without the time it sounds like now.

examples.en: I am meeting the carer tomorrow.
We are meeting the babysitter at six tomorrow.
We are visiting a car boot sale on Sunday.
They are meeting at the book club tonight.

fixes.wrong: I am meet the carer tomorrow.
fixes.right: I am meeting the carer tomorrow.

blocks.text: going to — you decided it yourself: I am going to renew my pass. -ing with a time — you have agreed it with someone, there is a date: We are paying for our membership on Friday. Both are about the future; the difference is whether there is an agreement.

examples.en: I am going to renew my pass.
I am bringing my appointment card tomorrow.
I am going to attend a christening.
We are attending a hen party on Saturday.

drill.why: There is an agreement and a time: am / is / are + -ing.

fixes.wrong: I going to descale the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

fixes.wrong: I am going descale the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

fixes.wrong: I am going to descaling the kettle.
fixes.right: I am going to descale the kettle.

blocks.text: going to is four parts: who + am / is / are + going + to, then the action as in the dictionary. Do not drop any of them.
Your own plan — am / is / are going to + action. You can see it coming — going to again. Agreed with someone, with a time — am / is / are + -ing + when.

examples.en: We are going to apply an undercoat.
The scarf is going to unravel.
They are meeting the cleaner tomorrow morning.
